previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for nausea, vomiting, abdominal bloating, and shortness of breath. She was found to have severe hyponatremia (Na 119) due to poor oral intake on a 'tea and toast' diet, exacerbated by gastroparesis and missed peritoneal dialysis. Her sodium improved with fluid restriction, solute supplementation, and daily manual dialysis. Constipation was severe despite a home bowel regimen; a CT scan showed significant stool burden. She responded well to soap suds enemas, which were taught for home use. Peritoneal fluid studies showed no infection. She was stabilized, discharged on her baseline medications, with instructions to resume her PD cycler, continue enemas, maintain fluid restriction, and follow up with nephrology and GI.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease

Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF SUMMARY STATEMENT
========================
Ms ___ is a ___ woman with a history of T1DM, ESRD on 
peritoneal dialysis, anxiety/depression, and fibromyalgia who 
presented with diffuse pain, especially localized in head, 
abdomen, and legs. Initial diagnostics were significant for a 
lipase of 200. UA and analysis of peritoneal fluid were 
negative. Physical exams during admission were significant for 
consistently reassuring abdominal exams, without localized pain, 
rebound, guarding, or peritoneal signs. Headaches were 
consistent with previous migraine pain, and leg and body pain 
was consistent with previous fibromyalgia pain. These were 
treated with her home medications. Since the patient had not had 
a bowel movement since ___, we initiated a rigorous bowel 
regimen that included her standard home regimen, plus Miralax, 
lactulose, and soap suds enemas. This resulted in a bowel 
movement on ___. As peritoneal dialysis had not been performed 
since ___, peritoneal dialysis was also performed on ___.

ACTIVE ISSUES
========================
# Abdominal pain -- Likely related to constipation, given 
reassuring serial exams since admission as well as negative UA 
and peritoneal fluid analysis. CT A/P on prior admission on 
___ with no evidence of pancreatitis. She was treated with 
an aggressive bowel regimen, with recommendations from renal. 
She will follow up with a gastroenterologist, since this was her 
second admission in 4 weeks for abdominal pain and discomfort 
related to constipation.

# headaches -- these resolved to her baseline over the course of 
her admission, they felt like her typical migraines, no focal 
neurological signs, no neck stiffness, no fever. She was 
continued on home sumatriptan Succinate ___ mg PO PRN

# leg pain and fibromyalgia -- no signs of trauma/falls, no 
focal neurological findings, pain is consistent with her typical 
fibromyalgia pain. No concerns for DVT or cellulitis. She was 
continued on home meds including Nortriptyline 10 mg PO/NG QHS, 
Pregabalin 75 mg PO/NG DAILY, Tizanidine 12 mg PO/NG QHS, and 
Tylenol as above   

# diabetes: Pt with T1DM, last A1C 6.7: She continued on insulin 
sliding scale

# anxiety/depression: Was tearful throughout her visit. Social 
work, spiritual care team, and primary care team were aware of 
her concerns and frustration with long term illness. She was 
continued on her home psych meds and will follow up with her 
PCP, ___, and psychiatrist.

# CODE STATUS: Since pt had mentioned to multiple members of her 
care team and to the spiritual care team that she wished to be 
DNR/DNI, we discussed goals of care and completed a MOLST. The 
purposes of the MOLST were explained, and pt was told that it 
would become part of her medical record. Pt confirmed that she 
did not want to be resuscitated if her heart should stop, and 
that she did not want to be intubated. She indicated that she 
would still wish to be hospitalized. Pt signed the MOLST form, 
and after being added to her medical record, it was sent home 
with her discharge paperwork. She will follow up with this issue 
with her primary care team.

CHRONIC ISSUES
========================
# renal disease - received peritoneal dialysis on ___ and ___ 
and was followed by renal. After dialysis, she felt better, with 
improvement in her malaise.

# hypercholesterolemia: continued Atorvastatin 40 mg PO/NG QPM

# hypothyroidism:  contd Levothyroxine Sodium 88 mcg PO/NG DAILY

# GERD:  contd home Pantoprazole 40 mg PO Q12H    

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
==============================
1. Follow up with PCP
2. Follow up with GI regarding chronic constipation.
